dsh-skill-invocation-monitor
English | 简体中文

> A **read-only** DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that puts
> every skill invocation on one screen: wh

ich Agents are running, which Skill each one is calling,
> whether it is running / finished / failed
, and how long it has been going — live, in the Web GUI sidebar.
*Captured from the running plugin: the sidebar entry opens a panel listing every Agent, and each row

is one
skill call with its status, elapsed time and start clock.*
## What changes after you install it
Skill invocation in DSH is invisible. The model loads a skill, and you see the answer — not the call

, not
the timing, not the one that never came back. After installing this plugin:
- the sidebar gains a **技能监控 / Skill Monitor** entry, with a live badge showing how many calls are r

unning;
- the panel lists every live Agent, and under each one every skill call with its **status**

and **elapsed time**;
- **both** ways a skill can be reached are covered and told apart — the model

calling the `skill` tool, and
**you** triggering a skill yourself, which carries a `用户触发` badge on i

ts row;
- nothing is written anywhere: no tool registered, no session state touched, no call interce
g is written anywhere: no tool registered, no session state touched, no call intercepted or delayed.

## Features

| Live Agent list | Every live Agent, its session title, and whether it is running or idle |
| Per-c

all rows | Skill name, status (`运行中` / `已完成` / `失败` / `未观测到结果`), elapsed time, start clock |
| Both

invocation paths | The model's `skill` tool call, and a human triggering a skill — marked `用户触发` |
|

Ticking durations | The elapsed time updates every second while a call is running |
| Sidebar badge
| The running-call count sits on the sidebar entry, so you can see activity without opening the pan

el |
| Honest failures | A failed call shows a truncated reason, e.g. `skill "…" is unknown or no lo

nger available` |
| Self-check diagnostics | Every response carries counters describing what the plu

gin observed, so a wrong assumption is visible rather than silent |
| Zero dependencies | Neither ha
lf imports a third-party package (the browser half uses only `react` from the host module table) |
## Permissions and data
This plugin exists to observe, and its whole design is built around not participating.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility
| DSH | Verified against **0.2.0-rc.2** (the build this plugin was developed and tested on). The sea

ms it uses are documented core surfaces, so other 0.2.x builds are expected to work |
| Node.js | De
clared `>=20`. The plugin runs inside the DSH host, so the host's own Node requirement is what matte

rs |
| Surface | Web GUI (`dsh.client.platform: "web"`). Uses only official Slots — `sidebar.panelli

st` for the entry and `main` for the panel — never DOM injection |
| Skill paths | Uses the durable
contracts for both paths: tool calls on `tools/pre-execute` / `tools/result`, and human invocations
through the `skill-invocation` message source declared by the skills seam |
## How it works
The two invocation paths — and why the human one is read from a message source
A skill can be reached two structurally different ways in DSH, and the plugin observes both.
| | Model path | User path |

| Trigger | The model calls the `skill` tool | You invoke a skill (e.g. `/grill-me`) |
| What DSH do
es | Runs the tool pipeline and produces a tool result | Appends the skill's instructions to the con

versation as a `user/message` — **no tool call and no command event** |
| Pairing key | `callId` | t

he message `id` |
| Duration measured | `tools/result` − `pre-execute` | `turn/end` − injection (see

the note below) |
| Row marker | none | `用户触发` |

The human path is read from the structured source the skills seam itself attaches
(`SkillInvocationS
ource`, in the persistence catalog):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The name comes straight from `source.name`, so no skill-catalog lookup and no text parsing is involv

ed. That
is a measured result, not a guess: an earlier implementation assumed the human path went th

rough
`command/run` / `command/done`, and a real session log disproved it — a human-invoked skill pr

oduces no
command event at all, which removed an entire catalog cache and its 60-second TTL.
**One deliberate choice:** a human skill has no result event of its own, so its duration is the *tur

n window*
(injection until `turn/end`), not the skill's own execution time. That is a stated convent

ion, not a
measurement — if you would rather see an instantaneous event with a duration of 0, only t

he settling point
changes.
Status semantics
| Status | Meaning |
| `运行中` | A start was observed (a pre-execute or a skill message) and no ending event has arrived; t

he duration grows live |
| `已完成` | The tool reported `isError === false`, or the turn that carried t

he skill ended normally |
| `失败` | The tool reported `isError === true`; the row shows a truncated r

eason |
| `未观测到结果` | No ending event arrived within 15 minutes (the call was denied before dispatch,
its parent was cancelled, the host crashed). This is a *derived* status and is never written back i
cancelled, the host crashed). This is a *derived* status and is never written back into the record |
